llm.summary: The skill's Notion-focused purpose matches its declared Notion API key and Node dependence, but its runtime instructions ask the agent to read local config files and execute local/other-skill scripts that are not included in the bundle — this broadens what will be accessed and should be reviewed before install.

dimensions.detail: Name/description describe Notion-based long-term memory and journaling; the declared primary env (NOTION_API_KEY) and required binary (node) align with that purpose. Declared dependency on a 'notion-api-automation' skill is plausible for implementing Notion operations.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to run local Node scripts (e.g., skills/soul-in-sapphire/scripts/*.js) and to execute scripts from another skill (scripts/notionctl.mjs). The skill metadata also lists localReads for ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json and ~/.config/soul-in-sapphire/config.json. Because this bundle contains no code files, the instructions assume and will act on files in the agent/user workspace and other skills—this expands the attack surface (file reads, child processes, and arbitrary local script execution) beyond the simple Notion API calls described.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec; this is instruction-only. That is lower risk than downloading/extracting remote binaries. However, runtime execution of local scripts still means code on disk (outside this bundle) will be executed.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only NOTION_API_KEY is declared (primaryEnv), which is appropriate for a Notion LTM skill. But SKILL.md references reading local config files (~/.openclaw/openclaw.json and ~/.config/soul-in-sapphire/config.json) and running other skill scripts—these files could contain additional secrets or paths. The skill does not request unrelated cloud credentials, which is good, but local file reads weaken that proportionality.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill is user-invocable; it does not request permanent/system-wide privileges. Autonomous invocation is allowed (default) which increases blast radius if the skill is later used autonomously, but that is a platform default and not in itself unexpected here.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to do what it says (Notion LTM) and only needs NOTION_API_KEY and node, but its instructions will: 1) read local config files (~/.openclaw/openclaw.json and ~/.config/soul-in-sapphire/config.json) and 2) execute local Node scripts and a separate 'notion-api-automation' script via child processes. Before installing or enabling: 

- Inspect the referenced local scripts (skills/soul-in-sapphire/scripts/*.js and scripts/notionctl.mjs) and the listed config files to confirm they exist and contain no secrets you don't want read or transmitted. The skill bundle does not include those scripts, so ensure they come from a trusted source. 
- Limit the NOTION_API_KEY scope (least privilege) and consider using a separate Notion integration account. Rotate the key if you later suspect misuse. 
- Verify what the dependent skill 'notion-api-automation' does and whether it requires other credentials. 
- If you cannot review the local scripts/configs, run the skill in a sandboxed environment or reject installation. 

These steps will reduce the risk that the agent executes or exposes local secrets when following the skill's instructions.
